headline: Intel and Qualcomm have reportedly raised the prices of their computer processors, and AMD may follow, as the cost of making advanced chips climbs.
score_reason: Kept at 6: the headline is properly hedged and matches the article; it rests on Taiwanese press reports and supply-chain sources, so it is not raised.
importance_line: Buyers of new laptops and PCs could pay more as chip makers pass on higher manufacturing costs, but the increases come from press reports and supply-chain sources rather than company announcements, and AMD's plans are unconfirmed.
summary: Commercial Times reports, as relayed by TrendForce, that Intel has reportedly raised prices on its PC processors by up to 20 percent since 1 Sep 2026 and, citing supply-chain sources, that Qualcomm raised prices on its Snapdragon X laptop chips by about 10 percent in October, while AMD is reportedly preparing increases whose size and timing are unconfirmed. The reports link the rises to demand for AI computers and to costlier production at TSMC, the Taiwanese contract chipmaker that makes these processors, which Central News Agency says analysts expect to charge 5 to 10 percent more for advanced chips in 2027.
notes: Read in full on TrendForce, which relays Commercial Times and Central News Agency; the Commercial Times original was not opened, so the url is the TrendForce page. The Intel rises date from 1 Sep 2026 and Qualcomm's from October, but this is the first time our editions carry the story, so it is marked NEW.
